newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer says Buba rate moves independent from US.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says Buba rate moves independent from US.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday that the central bank kept a watchful eye on interest rate developments in the U.S. but made its own decisions independently.
"Whatever is decided in the U.S., we watch," Tietmeyer said. "But our decisions are reached independently."
The Bundesbank chief added: "You can believe us that we continue to be sovereign in our decision making process."

Tietmeyer was responding to a question on whether Germany would now feel pressure to alter its monetary policy after the U.S. Federal Reserve ended its two-year easing cycle on March 25, raising the Fed funds target rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent.
He was speaking at a news conference following a regular policy-setting council meeting.
